hypothesis: Learn a query-dependent historical neighborhood instead of compressing all historical outcomes into a parametric classifier. A date-excluded soft-neighbor objective may recover nonlinear local structure that the completed neural, tree and sequence families missed. Public tabular benchmarks motivate this test but do not establish market accuracy.
partition: Reuse all original historical stride-four rows from d-5 through d-2. Previous-day noon alone selects an epoch. Preserve all 7070 original noon assessment queries per asset/date. Verify actual outcome release clocks before each historical/validation partition. These are exposed development dates, not independent confirmation.
preprocessing: Reuse the corresponding frozen historical neural model's exact column order, active-column mask and quantile-normal transform. Append its original -1/+1 asset indicator. Historical preprocessing has no assessment or validation fitting. No additional numerical embedding or feature selection is added in this family.

architectures.fixed_metric: Identity embedding of the frozen normalized inputs; no trainable parameters or epoch selection.
architectures.linear_nca: One bias-free linear map from normalized inputs to 128 coordinates. No output normalization or dimension-dependent distance rescaling.
architectures.nonlinear_nca: Linear(input,128), then BatchNorm1d(128), Linear(128,256), ReLU, Dropout(.1), Linear(256,128), BatchNorm1d(128). No residual connection. Batch normalization uses running statistics in evaluation.
architectures.parametric: Exactly the nonlinear_nca encoder followed by Linear(128,3). In training, pass the same concatenated query and sampled-bank inputs through the encoder, then apply ordinary weighted cross-entropy only to query outputs. This matches architecture, training feature exposure, query order and bank sampling, but has lower compute cost and does not consume bank labels as prediction values. Sampling remains label-stratified in both cases.

distance: For retrieval, use exp(-sqrt(max(||z_query||^2+||z_key||^2-2 z_query dot z_key,0)+1e-12)) with temperature fixed at 1. The 1e-12 smooths the zero-distance derivative; no learned temperature, nearest-k truncation, approximate index or outcome-dependent query selection.
training_exclusion: A training query can retrieve only keys from its own asset and a different entire UTC calendar day. Exclude its whole day across both assets before normalization. Self and every same-day overlapping five-second target therefore have zero retrieval weight. Other historical training days can lie before or after the training query; this is a leave-one-date-out fitting objective, not a claim of online chronological fitting within the historical training set.
training_bank: At each optimizer step sample 128 unique rows without replacement from every historical date/asset/class cell, using a separate numpy generator seeded 20260908. Four dates, two assets and three classes give 3072 sampled rows; a query has 1152 eligible same-asset, other-day keys. Require all 24 cell counts to be at least 128; do not resize or sample with replacement. The same bank is shared across the current 1024 queries and encoded together with them once, so train-time batch-normalization statistics are shared.
key_weights: Let n[d,a,c] be full historical cell counts. For query date e and asset a, each sampled key from d != e of class c has weight n[d,a,c] / (128 * sum_{r != e} n[r,a,c]). Thus the eligible sample's total weight is exactly one per class. This recovers the time mixture of the original class-conditional empirical bank rather than giving each day equal mass. For validation and assessment, use every historical key from the query asset, each with weight 1 / sum_r n[r,a,c]. All training keys are historical and released before those queries. Class scores are weighted kernel sums, normalized across the three classes. The stratified class sums are unbiased kernel-sum estimates; their normalized ratio and negative logarithm are not claimed unbiased.
query_objective: Use mean weighted negative log probability over each natural-order shuffled query minibatch. A row in asset/class (a,c) has fixed weight N/(6*n[a,c]), matching the original equal-asset/equal-class empirical objective. For retrieval, gradients pass through both query and sampled-key encoders. All future assessment outcomes are absent from fitting and model checkpoint interfaces.
epoch_selection: After every complete epoch, embed the entire historical key bank in evaluation mode and score both original previous-noon validation cohorts. Select the largest mean balanced accuracy using the original historical priors as decision denominator; ties use lower mean natural log loss, then the earlier epoch. Do not use assessment or same-day outcomes. Fixed metric has no trained epoch.
probability_semantics: Retrieval and parametric q represent the class-balanced fitting target. Return p_c proportional to q_c*pi[a,c], using the exact original full-history natural class prior. This is the same ideal class-prior recovery convention as the existing models, not proof that either q or p is calibrated. Retrieve within asset while sharing trainable encoder parameters across assets.
inference: Use full historical keys, streamed in chunks of 8192, with query batches of 256 and stable per-class log-sum-exp accumulation. No gradient, query-to-query attention, query labels or online bank updates. BatchNorm is in evaluation mode. Store the frozen encoder and precomputed key embeddings/labels/assets, validate persistence, and compare alternative query and key chunk partitions within a preflight-frozen tolerance.
fixed_blends: Average each of the eight new sources 50/50 with its original matched HGB (observations_tree or combined_hgb) and with deep500_hgb, giving sixteen blends. Retain all 184 completed feature-budget-family sources without changing forecasts. No blend-weight search.
backend_preflight: After the current transformer family completes, benchmark every architecture on synthetic 221- and 400-column inputs on two-thread CPU and available MPS, with the exact 1024-query/3072-bank training step and a 172800-row historical inference bank. Freeze repetitions, resource limits, timing projection, correctness tolerances and source hashes in a separate protocol before running any synthetic timing or market fit. Select one common feasible backend from numerical checks and a fixed total-time projection, never from accuracy. Preserve failed attempts. Do not purchase compute or relax limits implicitly.
verification: Test weighted kernels against independent explicit calculations, class-duplication invariance, exact other-date exclusion, stratified importance-weight totals, analytic/autograd gradients, full-bank streaming equivalence, future/prefix independence, evaluation-mode normalization, exact checkpoint round trips and source/prior/row identity. Run all three development dates before revealing any assessment score. Compare the complete procedure against the strongest retained control, and report per-asset and per-date effects before deciding whether independent confirmation is justified.

primary_sources.scope: ICLR 2025 ModernNCA: soft historical-neighbor prediction, learned linear/nonlinear embeddings, log-loss fitting, stochastic training neighborhoods and full-bank inference. Its final default uses Euclidean distance. Our date exclusion, class weighting, no-PLR architecture and fixed small training budget are deliberate differences; this is not a paper replication.

Official implementation inspected for architecture and training/inference distinctions. We implement the registered temporal and weighting variant independently rather than importing this mutable repository.
TabR, ICLR 2024, motivates learned retrieval. Its target-value transformation and nearest-neighbor residual architecture are not implemented in this family.
